{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Royal Concierge''' is the codename of a secret [[Government Communications Headquarters|GCHQ]] programme that watches the bookings made at select hotels worldwide.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.spiegel.de/international/europe/gchq-monitors-hotel-reservations-to-track-diplomats-a-933914.html|title='Royal Concierge': GCHQ Monitors Hotel Reservations to Track Diplomats|last=Poitras|first=Laura|author2=Marcel Rosenbach |author3=Holger Stark |date=2013-11-17|publisher=Spiegel|accessdate=17 November 2013}}</ref> The programme was introduced in 2010 and monitored 350 hotels around the world. The system alerted GCHQ to a diplomat's travel arrangements and allowed GCHQ to bug rooms in preparation for the diplomat's arrival.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-11-17 |title=Snowden cache reveals diplomats' hotel bookings being tracked by GCHQ |url=http://www.theguardian.com/world/2013/nov/17/edward-snowden-diplomats-hotel-bookings-documents |access-date=2023-01-30 |website=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref>
